sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cathleen ni Houlihan, also written Caitlín Ní hUallacháin, is an Irish name for the sovereignty goddess. The title grew known through a play. W. B. Yeats wrote the play of that title. Actress and activist Maud Gonne performed the role of Cathleen. In the drama a poor old woman turns into a queen. That change echoes the older tales of the Cailleach.

okr.objective: Cathleen ni Houlihan is Yeats's name for the sovereignty of Ireland.
key_results: It is an Irish name for the sovereignty goddess.
Yeats wrote a well-known play of the same title.
Maud Gonne played Cathleen on the stage.
Her poor old woman doubles as a monarch, echoing the Cailleach.
